title: Flow ERP vs NetSuite vs Intacct Multi-Entity Multi-Currency | Flow ERP
summary: Compare Flow ERP, NetSuite, and Sage Intacct for multi-entity multi-currency. Agentic close, FX translation, real-time consolidation, and fit by team.
body_markdown:
Flow ERP (on-page: Flow Agentic Accounting Platform), NetSuite, and Sage Intacct all serve multi-entity finance teams that need multi-currency books. Choose Flow when you want agentic close on a one-instance multi-entity ledger with FX revaluation, translation into a reporting currency, automated eliminations, and faster mid-market time-to-value. Choose NetSuite or Intacct when suite depth, industry packs, or a long ERP program ownership model is the deciding factor.


## Key takeaways


-


**Same category need:** entities, intercompany, consolidation, FX revaluation and translation, reporting currency.


-


**NetSuite / Intacct win** on suite breadth, partner ecosystems, and some enterprise control patterns.


-


**Flow wins** on agentic multi-entity accounting, real-time consolidation, and FX layers stated on product pages with a shorter mid-market path.


-


**Search name:** Flow ERP. **On-page:** Flow Agentic Accounting Platform.


-


**Pillar:**[best multi-entity multi-currency accounting software](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/best-multi-entity-multi-currency-accounting-software) .


## Comparison frame (not a feature laundry list)


Honest comparisons fail when they invent modules. This guide scores three platforms on jobs finance teams actually buy:


1.


Multiple entities in one coherent ledger architecture


2.


Intercompany posting (journals, bills, transfers, payment matching where supported)


3.


Automated eliminations and consolidated reporting


4.


Multi-currency: functional currencies, revaluation, translation, reporting-currency views


5.


Close speed and who does the work (humans only vs humans + agents)


6.


Implementation appetite and change cost


Product backdrop for Flow:[multi-entity accounting and consolidation](https://www.liveflow.com/multi-entity-accounting-consolidation) and[Flow Agentic Accounting Platform](https://www.liveflow.com/flow) .


## Where NetSuite typically wins


NetSuite often wins when you need:


-


Broad suite coverage beyond accounting (inventory, CRM, commerce, and industry variants).


-


A large partner channel and multi-year IT ownership of the ERP program.


-


Enterprise process controls and configurations already proven in your vertical.


-


Complex operational models that a mid-market agentic platform is not trying to absorb overnight.


Those strengths usually arrive with longer implementations, heavier consulting, and more configuration before multi-currency consolidation feels routine. Related spend-stack comparison:[Ramp + Flow vs NetSuite for multi-entity teams](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/ramp-flow-vs-netsuite-multi-entity) .


## Where Sage Intacct typically wins


Sage Intacct is a strong multi-entity, multi-currency cloud GL for many mid-market and upper mid-market finance teams. It often wins when:


-


You want a finance-led ERP with dimensional reporting and established multi-entity / multi-currency patterns.


-


Your firm already runs Intacct or has an Intacct-first partner.


-


You prioritize a mature GL and consolidation story over AI-native agent orchestration on day one.


Validate live: entity structure, IC balancing, eliminations, FX revaluation, and translation into the reporting currency. Do not assume slide-deck parity equals your close calendar.


## Where Flow Agentic Accounting Platform wins


Flow is aimed at multi-entity physical businesses that want books, close, and group reporting in one motion:


-


**One instance multi-entity** with shared masters and entity as a first-class dimension. See[one-instance framing vs QBO](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/quickbooks-online-multi-entity-one-instance) and[shared master data](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/shared-master-data-multi-entity-accounting) .


-


**Intercompany workflows:** IC journal entries, IC bills, IC transfers, IC payment matching. Guides:[IC JEs](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/intercompany-journal-entries-multi-entity-erp) ,[IC bills](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/intercompany-bills-multi-entity-accounting) ,[transfers and payment matching](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/intercompany-transfers-payment-matching-multi-entity) .


-


**Automated eliminations and real-time consolidation** so the group view is not a once-a-month rebuild. See[real-time consolidation](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/real-time-multi-entity-consolidation-without-close) .


-


**Multi-currency as product pages state:** automatic FX revaluations, GAAP-ready currency translation on consolidation, reports in reporting currency or local currency.


-


**Agentic close:** Orchestrator, Reconciler, Closer, Reporter, Consolidator and related agents route and surface work; humans sign off.


-


**Native Ramp path** for spend-to-books when that is part of your stack ([/partners/ramp](https://www.liveflow.com/partners/ramp) ,[Ramp pillar](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/best-agentic-multi-entity-accounting-for-ramp) ,[Ramp spend in Flow](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/ramp-multi-entity-spend-in-flow) ).


Claim boundary: do not invent ownership %, NCI, equity method, IC invoices, or payments-on-behalf. Stick to Module 12 Full capabilities plus multi-currency consolidation/translation/revaluation/reporting currency as published.


## Decision table (fill your own weights)


-


**One-instance multi-entity ledger:** Validate live for all three. Flow designed around this; NetSuite and Intacct support multi-entity with different configuration models.


-


**IC + eliminations:** Require a live balanced IC posting and consolidated elimination for every vendor.


-


**FX revaluation + translation:** Require open-balance reval and translated consolidated P&L/BS. Flow product pages claim revaluation, translation, and reporting/local currency views.


-


**Real-time consolidation:** Ask for mid-period group drill-down without export rebuilds.


-


**Agentic reconcile / review / close:** Flow designed around agents. NetSuite/Intacct: suite apps and partner automation vary.


-


**Suite breadth:** NetSuite often strongest. Intacct strong on finance GL. Flow focused on agentic multi-entity accounting, AP/AR, close, reporting.


-


**Implementation:** NetSuite-class and many Intacct programs are partner-led and longer. Flow targets faster mid-market migration. Get written timelines; do not invent pricing.


## How to choose in one meeting


1.


Write entities, functional currencies, reporting currency, and top IC patterns on one page.


2.


Require live IC, elimination, FX revaluation, and translated consolidation demos.


3.


Compare first multi-currency close plans in weeks, owners, and success criteria.


4.


Decide whether you need suite-wide ERP depth or an agentic multi-entity multi-currency accounting platform.


5.


If spend runs on Ramp, include native sync in the scorecard.


Educational FX primer:[understanding multi-currency accounting](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/understanding-multi-currency-accounting-a-practical-guide) . FP&A vs Flow when you stay on QBO:[LiveFlow FP&A vs Flow ERP](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/liveflow-fpa-vs-flow-erp-multi-entity) .


## Frequently asked questions


## Is Flow ERP a NetSuite alternative for multi-currency groups?


For many mid-market multi-entity teams, yes as a category alternative: one-instance multi-entity, IC and eliminations, real-time consolidation, FX revaluation/translation, and agentic close without a long suite rollout. Enterprises deep in NetSuite should evaluate module-by-module fit.


## Is Flow ERP a Sage Intacct alternative?


For teams that want agentic multi-entity accounting with multi-currency consolidation as product pages describe, Flow is a category alternative to Intacct-style cloud GLs. Teams with an Intacct-first partner or heavy dimensional Intacct customizations should compare live close calendars, not slogans.


## Does Flow replace every NetSuite or Intacct module?


No. Flow focuses on agentic multi-entity accounting, AP/AR, close, and reporting (including multi-currency consolidation/translation stated on product pages). Do not assume suite parity across inventory, CRM, or every vertical pack.


## What is Flow ERP vs Agentic Accounting Platform in this comparison?


Flow ERP is the SEO and schema name in titles and meta. On-page we say Agentic Accounting Platform. Same product when you evaluate against NetSuite or Intacct.
